components.css: .ds-work-card { display: flex; flex-direction: column; gap: 1rem; text-decoration: none; } .ds-work-card-frame { position: relative; aspect-ratio: 4/5; overflow: hidden; border-radius: 1.5rem; background: #1a1a1a; box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.1); } .ds-work-card-img { position: absolute; inset: 0; width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: cover; transition: transform 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1), filter 0.7s cubic-bezier(0.22,1,0.36,1); } .ds-work-card:hover .ds-work-card-img, .ds-work-card:focus-visible .ds-work-card-img { transform: scale(1.05); filter: brightness(1.06); } .ds-work-card:focus-visible .ds-work-card-frame { box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 2px #f58b27; } .ds-work-card-name { display: block; font-family: Poppins, sans-serif; font-weight: 700; font-size: 1rem; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.9); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; } .ds-work-card-dot { color: #f58b27; } .ds-work-card-meta { display: block; font-family: Poppins, sans-serif; font-weight: 500; font-size: 0.875rem; color: rgba(255,255,255,0.65); white-space: nowrap; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; }

narrative.overview: Propagenda's surfaces read as a black-and-orange proof reel for an agency, not a portfolio brochure: dark charcoal/black grounds, real client imagery pushed forward, and a single orange accent used the way a wire-service editor uses a terminal period — rarely, and only to close a thought. Density breathes in alternating beats (a dense image beat, a quiet type beat, dense again) rather than holding one register for the whole scroll. Scroll length tracks the amount of real content a page has; nothing is padded out with a locked-viewport pin or an extra full-screen stop just to look expensive.
keyCharacteristics: Black/charcoal ground, one orange accent, near-black text on orange
Poppins throughout, plain sentence case, no second/mono voice
Depth via gradient scrims, blurred color glows, and opacity layering — no drop shadows
Sections alternate image-dense and type-quiet; scroll length matches real content
Real client assets (photos, logos, quotes) are the differentiator, never placeholder art

rules.name: The Ink-on-Orange Rule
rules.body: Any text sitting on the orange accent surface uses ink (#141414), never white. White-on-orange measures 2.44:1 and is banned outright.

rules.name: The Punctuation Rule
rules.body: Orange marks a single terminal point per composition (a period, an accent bar, one numeral, one glow) — it is never the dominant color of a screen in this template.

rules.name: The One-Face Rule
rules.body: Poppins is brand law; expression is weight and scale only, never a second family or a mono/tracked-caps register (retired site-wide 2026-09-15).

rules.name: The No-Eyebrow Rule
rules.body: No label sits above its content as a separate small-caps or tracked line — this is a structural ban, not just a styling one. A stage or figure's name folds inline into its own sentence or heading instead.

rules.name: The No-Hero-Metric Rule
rules.body: Results never render as one giant figure over a small label, nor as a grid of smaller supporting stat tiles. Every value/label pair reads at the same scale.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: Depth comes from light (scrims, blurred glows) and translucency (bordered dividers), never from a cast box-shadow.

rules.name: The Cover-Never-Gated Rule
rules.body: A cover image, once a project has one, is visible at rest at every breakpoint including touch. Hover/focus states may only lift or brighten an already-visible cover; they may never be the sole mechanism that reveals it.

rules.name: The Auto-Fit Density Rule
rules.body: A dense card wall uses grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min,max)) with justify-content: center, not a fixed grid-cols-N, so column count adapts to viewport width and a short group centers its row instead of stranding empty track.

dos: Do keep Poppins as the only family across every register; vary weight and size, never the face.
Do use ink (#141414) for any text on an orange surface.
Do fold a stage or figure's name inline into its own sentence instead of stacking a label above content.
Do let scroll-linked motion ride a section's natural height (scrub against the section's own start/end) rather than pinning the viewport to extend page length.
Do ground recurring backdrop moments (like the pull quote) in the subject's own real asset before falling back to a generic brand pattern.
donts: Don't use a kicker/eyebrow label above content anywhere on the public site — the ban is structural (no label-above-content composition), not only a styling rule about mono.
Don't render a stat/result as one giant figure over a small label, or as a row of smaller stat tiles — this is the banned hero-metric template.
Don't put white text on the orange accent surface (2.44:1, fails contrast).
Don't reintroduce font-mono or an uppercase/tracked "backstage" register anywhere (site-wide directive, 2026-09-15) without a fresh, explicit decision.
Don't add a cast box-shadow for depth; use scrims, blurred glow blooms, or translucent borders instead.
